articles.headline: Personal Items: Rev. R. P. Gibbs of Union A.M.E. Church ill
articles.summary: Rev. R. P. Gibbs, Pastor of Union A. M. E. Church of this city, has been very sick for two weeks, with pleurisy. He has been under the care of a doctor, and most of the time confined to his room. He is slowly improving. During his illness, he has been cheered by the manifestations of sympathy and unremitting attention of the members of his church.

articles.headline: It is Invaluable (editorial endorsement of the Macamoose Tonic)
articles.summary: It is invaluable.--We do not generally recommend medicines in our editorial columns, but having lately used the "Macamoose Tonic," prepared by Rev. I. R. Gates, and found it such a great remedy for Bronchitis and sore throat, as well as a blood purifier... For sale at 1230 Wood St. and 1613 [VERIFY: 1613 or 1618] North 11th St.
people: preparer of the Macamoose Tonic (Rev.); 1230 Wood St. and 1613 [VERIFY] North 11th St.

Brown, agent, who will let them have them for a reasonable amount. Persons living at a distance, North or South, can have their likenesses, or those of their friends, sent to them, by paying the cost... James W. Brown, No. 14 South Sixth Street, Philadelphia. articles.headline: The Great Union Fair (rewards and prizes)
articles.summary: The Great Union Fair, in aid of our Book Concern and paper... The ladies are progressing. Rewards and prizes: three silver cups to the lady or gentleman collecting the largest sums, forwarded to the President or Vice-President of the Association appointed by four of our Philadelphia churches; returns by November 1st.

articles.headline: Personal Items: Rev. R. H. Cain leaves for Charleston; E. D. Bassett to lecture at Charleston
articles.summary: Rev. R. H. Cain and family left our city for New York, en route for Charleston, S.C., on Thursday last. Bro. Cain has greatly intensified the interest already felt in the missionary work by the very encouraging report which he has made... (Editorial items:) The Charleston Journal says that E. D. Bassett of our city has accepted an invitation to lecture before the Y. M. L. A. of that city this fall.
people: missionary to South Carolina; left Philadelphia with family for Charleston via New York, c. 1866-10-11 (Rev.)
of Philadelphia; to lecture at Charleston this fall

articles.headline: A.M.E. Church news: Philadelphia (Bethel missionary Sabbath; Union Church; Zion Mission revival)
articles.summary: Philadelphia.--Bethel A.M.E. Church was the scene of much interest on last Sabbath. Rev. J. M. Brown preached in the morning, and Rev. R. H. Cain in the afternoon. Great interest in the missionary cause was created... Union Church was favored with the presence of the Missionary Secretary, who succeeded in collecting about twenty-five dollars. Rev. R. P. Gibbs, the pastor, is again partially restored to health. Zion Mission Church is still enjoying a gracious revival; over fifty have been added to the membership.

articles.headline: Obituary: Ann Coonell [VERIFY] of Wesley Church; Sister Morgan
articles.author: J. P. H.
articles.summary: Ann Coonell [VERIFY] was born near Stanton, Delaware, November 26th, 1824. She had been a resident of Philadelphia since 1844. She was converted and joined Wesley Church, in '55 or '56. She was taken sick on Wednesday evening of last week... Being desirous of seeing her class leader, Brother Hookinson [VERIFY]... To Mr. Isaac Williams she said... To Brother Woolford... on Friday night... she passed into that sleep in Jesus. Zion Standard please copy. Also Sister Morgan, one of the oldest members of the Church, departed this life on the 8th inst.
people: deceased; b. near Stanton, Del., 1824-11-26; Philadelphia resident since 1844; member of Wesley Church

articles.headline: Personal Items: Miss Mary Still sails for Savannah; Mrs. Mary Augusta Johnson teaching at Woodbury
articles.summary: Miss Mary Still, the faithful missionary to the Freedmen of South Carolina, sailed for Savannah on last Saturday. She was accompanied by two young ladies, who go out to assist her. Her soul seems to be in this great work, and her labors are greatly blessed... Mrs. Mary Augusta Johnson, wife of Professor Johnson, the celebrated blind lecturer, is teaching school at Woodbury, N.J.
people: missionary to the Freedmen of South Carolina; sailed for Savannah c. 1866-10-13 (printed 'Miss Mary Still')
teacher, Woodbury, N.J.; wife of Professor Johnson, the blind lecturer

articles.headline: The Fair (Union Fair, Philadelphia) and 'Attention! Read!'
articles.summary: We wish to say a word to our Philadelphia ladies in reference to the great Union Fair to be held in Philadelphia for two successive weeks, commencing on the first of November. Mrs. Hallwell [VERIFY] and the Vice-Presidents of the Union Fair are working nearly every night in the week... They have got representatives from all the colored churches in the city. There are also young ladies engaged from each of the colored churches to attend the tables... a table at the end of the Hall to be called the President and Vice-President's table. (Also 'Attention! Read!': ministers of the Philadelphia and New York Districts to set their congregations to work; articles to Elisha Weaver, No. 631 Pine street, by Nov 1-2.)

articles.headline: Zion Mission A.M.E. Church (letter of the pastor; William Still's gift of coal)
articles.author: T. Gould
articles.summary: Mr. Editor:--When I received from the Bishop my appointment to Zion Mission A.M.E. church, located in Seventh street, below Dickerson, Philadelphia, Pa., I cheerfully entered upon my labors. The number of members was forty-five, and, as is generally the case, a great many of them could not be found... We now number ninety-one... I took occasion to call on my friend, Mr. Wm. Still, who is carrying on the coal business at 1216 Washington Avenue... He instantly informed me that he would send us a ton of coal gratis... if the Rev. Stephen Smith... would be so kind as to cancel the debt of two thousand dollars which this handful of people owe him... Philadelphia, Penna., October 9th, 1866.
people: coal dealer, 1216 Washington Avenue; donated a ton of coal to Zion Mission

articles.headline: Our Church in the City (Centenary services at Zion Mission and Union Bethel); Take Notice (Centenary collection)
articles.summary: Rev. Theodore Gould.--Zion Mission Church will have an interesting meeting on next Sabbath, for the benefit of the Centenary Fund. At 11 o'clock Rev. Elisha Weaver will deliver a discourse on 'Education.' At 3 o'clock, the pastor, Rev. Theodore Gould, will lecture on the 'Rise and Progress of Methodism.' At night Rev. F. P. Maion [VERIFY] will preach a sermon. Union Bethel Church, of which Rev. R. P. Gibbs is pastor, will be favored with a discourse in the evening, by Rev. Elisha Weaver. (Take Notice:) The coming Sabbath is the day set apart for the taking up of the great collection in honor of the centenary of Methodism in this country...
people: pastor, Zion Mission Church; Centenary lecture 1866-10-28 (Rev.)
Centenary discourses at Zion Mission and Union Bethel, 1866-10-28 (Rev.)

articles.headline: Union Fair: Special Notice (postponed to Nov 5 or 6), Representatives, and base ball prize
articles.summary: The 'Great Union Fair of the A.M.E. Book Concern and paper,' will be held in Liberty Hall, Lombard St., below Eighth, Philadelphia, on the 5th or 6th of November. The Fair was to be held on the 1st, but in consequence of the proprietors not having their hall ready, it will be held at the time appointed. Tickets will be good during the month... three handsome silver cups... (Representatives of the Union Fair in Philadelphia:) There will be a representation of sixteen churches in the fair held at Liberty Hall. Two or three ladies from each church will be appointed to wait on the tables. (Still Further Inducements:) the Committee have a complete set of Base Ball Implements to be awarded to the club having the largest number of votes; white and colored clubs of our city and elsewhere... send their names, with the address of their Corresponding Secretary, to Rev. Elisha Weaver, No. 631 Pine St. (office of the A.M.E. Book Store) where tickets of the fair can be obtained.
people: receives base-ball club entries; No. 631 Pine St., office of the A.M.E. Book Store (Rev.)

articles.headline: Rev. James Lynch, Editor, leaves on a Southern tour; Absent from the City
articles.summary: This gentleman left home on the 23d instant, on a tour through the South. We hope that all of our brethren who are indebted to the Concern will settle with him... Bro. Lynch is absent from the city, and is not expected back for six or eight weeks. We have the editorial charge of the paper this week... (Trip to Morristown:) Brother Lynch... is preparing for his grand Southern tour... He expects to visit the New Orleans Conference, over which Bishop Campbell now presides.
people: editor; left Philadelphia 1866-10-23 on a tour of the South (Rev.)

articles.headline: Obituaries: Abigail Barlow (Bethel); Geo. W. Elliot (Zion Mission); Wm. Henry Draper (Oxford, Chester Co.)
articles.summary: Departed this life on the 9th inst., Sister Abigail Barlow [printed 'Harlow' at first mention, 'Barlow' thereafter], consort of Dr. Barlow, a well-known and highly successful physician in our city. Sister Barlow was a member of Bethel Church for some thirty years... Her age was 64 [VERIFY]... She leaves behind her a husband, son, and many friends... Her remains were interred on the 13th inst. -- Departed this life on the 4th of October, 1866, in Centreville, Camden, New Jersey, Mr. Geo. W. Elliot, aged 26 years and 5 months. Bro. Elliot was born in Portsmouth, Virginia... He came to Philadelphia, and a short time after his advent here, he embraced religion, and became a member of Zion Mission Church. -- Wm. Henry Draper, son of Hannah and Elias P. Draper, of Oxford, Chester Co., departed this life Oct. 3d, 1866 (verses signed John W. Stevenson, Oxford, Pa.).

articles.summary: Address 'To the People of the United States' calling a National Convention of Colored Soldiers and Sailors to meet at Philadelphia, Pa., January 8th, 1867. Signed by Thomas R. articles.headline: A Trip to the Great West
articles.summary: Travel letter (byline initials read as 'W. E. W.' [VERIFY]): the writer, invited by the Wilberforce students' Society of Inquiry on Missions to its anniversary (Mon. Oct. 15), left Baltimore Sept. 28 by the Northern Central R.R.; describes the rebuilding of Wilberforce University (burned April 14, 1865) and its residents, then Chillicothe, Louisville and Cincinnati; 'On the Wing, Oct. 25, 1866.'

articles.headline: Home for Aged and Infirm Colored Persons, 340 South Front Street
articles.summary: The Home for Aged and Infirm Colored Persons, No. 340 South Front Street, established about three years ago, the late Maurice Hall its moving spirit; nineteen inmates aged 70 to 104. Every colored church is urged to take up a Sabbath collection for it.

articles.headline: Commencement and Examination of the Institute for Colored Youth
articles.summary: The fourteenth annual commencement of the Institute for Colored Youth at National Hall, Market street; examination of the higher classes in the Institute's own building; classical preceptors Mr. E. D. Bassett and Miss Fanny Jackson.

articles.headline: The Great Union Fair (opening Thursday the 15th; prizes)
articles.summary: The Great Union Fair will certainly open on Thursday the 15th inst. and continue about two weeks; sixteen or seventeen churches are represented; Mrs. Maria Hallowell is President, with four Vice-Presidents. Prizes on view at the book store, No. 631 Pine street: three silver cups for the three persons who raise the largest sums outside the committees; a silver-mounted hat for the club with most votes; a gilded ball; and the library register for the Sabbath School with the most votes.

articles.headline: Special Notice: To the Committee of the Union Fair
articles.author: Maria Hallowell

articles.headline: Examination of the Institute for Colored Youth
articles.summary: Report of the examination of the Institute for Colored Youth on Thursday and Friday, the 1st and 2d inst., at the building on Shippen street west of Ninth, and of the commencement at National Hall, Market street, before about three thousand people; four graduates received diplomas from Prof. Bassett.

articles.headline: The Colored People of Philadelphia
articles.summary: The colored people of Philadelphia are displaying a spirit of industry and enterprise not before exhibited: on every hand stores and shops of almost every description are being opened by them; tradesmen of almost every branch of industry are seen on the street daily; partnerships and associations are being formed.

articles.headline: The Union Fair (editorial)
articles.summary: The fair has been in progress for two weeks, under the control of Mrs Mary Hollowell [VERIFY], the President, assisted by the Vice Presidents Mrs Davis, Mrs Allen, Mrs. Hollensworth [VERIFY], and Miss Lankum [VERIFY], of Bethel, Wesley, Union and Zion Mission churches respectively, who have spared no pains to make it a complete success... in aid of the Book Concern.

articles.headline: Attention! Read! (Union Fair appeal)
articles.author: E. W.
articles.summary: Will not all the ministers in the Philadelphia and New York Districts be sure to set their congregations to work for the great Union Fair? Bishop Wayman has his eyes fixed on all of the ministers who have charge of circuits and stations... Send donations to Elisha Weaver, No. 619 Pine street.

articles.headline: A Great Work to Be Done (editorial; streetcars)
articles.summary: There is a great work to be done on the part of our people, both in Church and State... We have been excluded from the city cars for no other reason than that our hue is darker than that of those who claim to be our superiors... We are living in great hopes that the Supreme Court, which meets in December, will bring up, for decision, the question, whether a public conveyance has the right to exclude any person on account of color.

articles.headline: Church Union (editorial)
articles.summary: The Philadelphia, New York, and New England Conferences only hold one more session each, before the General Conference... We hope, at the next Annual Conference of the Philadelphia district, to be held in Bethel church, Philadelphia, to hear a general report from all our circuits and stations [on union of the A.M.E. and Zion A.M.E. Churches].

articles.headline: Donations to the Union Fair
articles.summary: In our issue of last week we failed to acknowledge the receipt of a present for the Fair, from the good people of Woodbury, N.J.... Rev Jacob Mitchell, in charge of Burlington Circuit, raised at Mount Holly, N.J., six dollars and fifteen cents... Rev Daniel Draper brought from his charge at Bridgeton, N.J., a pair of beautiful glass ships. The Sabbath School at Gouldtown, N.J., in the pastoral charge of the Rev Nelson H. Turpin, donated a small china tea-set... a fine cake from a lady of Camden, N.J., and one from a lady member of the Union Church of Philadelphia.
people: in charge of Burlington Circuit, raised $6.15 at Mount Holly (Rev.)

people: Superintendent of Bethel Sabbath School; assisted at the Fair

articles.headline: Colored Conventions (editorial; National Equal Rights League call to Washington)
articles.summary: The President of the National Equal Rights League has issued another call for the National Convention to be held in Washington, D.C., in January next. The last call invites the people to send delegates, instead of restricting the representation to regular organizations...

articles.headline: Concerts at the New Liberty Hall (local)

Cliff [VERIFY]... Prof. Lively... Macbeth by Mr M. R. Hunton [VERIFY] and Miss Josephine Sylvester. articles.headline: Letter from Brother Grimes: Gloucester County suffrage meeting

articles.summary: A public meeting of the colored citizens of Gloucester county was held in the A.M.E. Grimes; Vice President Joseph Andrews; Secretary John Andrews...

articles.headline: Institute for Colored Youth: correction re 'Mrs. H. G. Jones'
articles.author: E. D. Bassett

articles.author: C. V. B.
articles.summary: Philadelphia, Dec. 1866. A woman correspondent urges young people to canvass for the Sabbath schools and the church 'while she remains in this the City of Brotherly Love'.

articles.headline: Jottings by the Way: Evidences of Progress (Newark, New York, Brooklyn; Philadelphia streetcars and the soldiers)
articles.author: A. M. G.
articles.summary: Philadelphia, Dec. 15th, 1866. Notes of a tour among the churches of Newark, Orange, Morristown, New York and Brooklyn... On my return, I find our brave Boys in Blue here and hereabouts wide awake on the great issue of the day. Every effort is being made to give our late comrades in arms a fitting welcome to the city of Brotherly Love, which will no doubt be subjected to the disgrace of being recognized as the only city of the loyal North mean enough to practise this disgraceful exclusion of colored persons from her city passenger cars... the 8th of January will find some of our boys from abroad along these lines...

events.location: Richmond, Va. (speeches in front of the Lyceum, Washington Street)
events.description: Reprinted from the Virginia State Journal: 'The procession of colored Odd Fellows yesterday was a most handsome affair, and compared favorably with any thing ever witnessed by this community'; the strictest principles of propriety were observed. The speeches, delivered in front of the Lyceum, on Washington Street, by Past Grand Master Wm. P. Gibson, of Good Samaritan Lodge, Phila.; Jas. McCrommel, of Unity Lodge, Phila.; John C. Bowers, of Unity Lodge, Phila.; James Jordan, of Olive Lodge, Baltimore; and Past Noble Father Perpener, of Harmony Lodge, Alexandria, are represented as very able efforts. The ball at night proceeded with the greatest harmony. (Parade topic; the date is not given in the reprint.)
attendees: Past Grand Master, Good Samaritan Lodge, Philadelphia; speaker

events.name: Reunion and parade of colored soldiers, Woodstown, N.J. (Philadelphia band)
events.location: Bush town [as printed 'Bushtown'] A.M.E. Church and Woodstown, Salem Co., N.J.
events.description: Letter from New Jersey ('Great Reunion of Colored Soldiers -- Speeches of Revs. Grimes and Turpin'), signed A Spectator, Yorktown, N.J., Oct 8, 1866. On Sept 27 the colored soldiers of the late war residing in the vicinity met in front of Bushtown A.M.E. Church under Colonel C. H. Sullivan; Lieut. Colonel J. W. Sherkly; Major Wm. H. Werner; Adjutant J. A. Sullivan; Sergeant Major H. Groome; Chaplain Rev. Wm. W. Grimes; Captains M. M. Dent [?], G. Kelley and J. G. Sullivan. The battalion, headed by Professor Davis's band of Philadelphia, marched to a farm for muskets, drilled near Woodstown, and marched into Woodstown, the colored people marching two by two behind the soldiers to the town hall; speeches by Rev. J. D. Morris (pastor of the M.E. church at Woodstown) and Rev. N. H. Turpin; dinner at Mr. Thomas Johnson's [?]. 'The parade was a perfect success.' Parade topic; New Jersey names left in text except the Philadelphia Conference minister.

events.name: Zion Mission A.M.E. Church -- quarterly meeting
events.location: Zion Mission A.M.E. Church, Seventh St. below Dickerson, Philadelphia
events.description: Quarterly Meeting at Zion Mission (Rev. Theodore Gould, Pastor) on last Sabbath was characterized by an unusual religious interest; the revival meetings had just closed the week preceding. Rev. Stephen Smith preached in the morning; in the afternoon Rev. Mr. Miller, Pastor of the Scott M.E. church, preached 'Every body's Sermon', many of his congregation accompanying him; at night Rev. E. Weaver preached. Love Feast on Monday night crowded.

events.name: Union A.M.E. Church, Coates Street -- quarterly meeting
events.description: Quarterly Meeting will take place at Union church, Coates street, to-morrow, Sabbath, Oct 21st. At half-past 10 o'clock Rev. Theodore Gould will officiate; at 3 o'clock, Rev. Joseph Smith; at 8 o'clock [preacher not named]. Love Feast on Monday night. R. P. Gibbs, Pastor.

events.name: Wesley church, Hurst street -- special services
events.location: Wesley church, Hurst street, Philadelphia (Little Wesley)
events.description: At Wesley church, Hurst street, (Rev. Wm. Watson, pastor,) interesting services will take place to-morrow, Sabbath, October 21st. All the friends of Methodism are invited to attend. Eminent speakers are expected. (Hurst Street = Little Wesley, A.M.E., per owner ruling.)

events.name: Bristol circuit -- quarterly meetings (Bristol, Bensalem)
events.location: Bristol, Pa.; Bensalem, Pa.; and a third appointment (Nov 11)
events.description: Quarterly Meeting at Bristol, Pa., on Sabbath, Oct. 28th; at Bensalem, Pa., Sabbath, November 4th; at 'Harrisburg Hill [VERIFY], Pa.' Nov. 11th. Conference on Saturday previous to each meeting, at 2 o'clock P.M. Thomas M. Kinnard [VERIFY: Kinnaird?], Minister in charge.

events.name: Bethel A.M.E. Church -- extra meeting and quarterly meeting (Centenary week)
events.location: Bethel A.M.E. Church, Sixth Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Notice: There will be an extra meeting held at Bethel A.M.E. Church, Sixth Street, Philadelphia, to commence on the evening of the 23d inst., and to continue till Friday night, closing with a general class. On Sunday the 28th, Quarterly Meeting will be held. Special collections will be lifted for educational purposes, the Book Concern and superannuated preachers. Love feast on Monday night, 29th inst. James Hollen, Pastor. Oct 27--1t.

events.name: Zoar M.E. Church -- Sabbath services for the Daughters of Conference Fund
events.description: Notice: By Divine permission, on next Sabbath, the 28th inst., the Rev. J. P. Hamer, of Wesley Zion Church, will preach in Zoar M.E. Church, at 10 1/2 o'clock, A.M., Rev. R. H. Dyson, at 3 o'clock, P.M., and Rev. R. P. Gibbs, of the A.M.E. Church, at 7 1/2 o'clock. A special collection will be taken during the day for the Daughters of Conference Fund. J. H. Pearce, Minister in Charge. Oct 27--1t. ('Wesley Zion Church' = presumably Big Wesley, A.M.E. Zion, Lombard St.; flagged.)
attendees: minister in charge, Zoar M.E. Church

events.name: Union A.M.E. Church -- quarterly meeting
events.description: Quarterly Meeting at Union A.M.E. Church was a precious season, temporally and spiritually. $70 was raised to pay the salary of the pastor, Rev. R. P. Gibbs. (Report of the meeting announced Oct 20 for Sunday Oct 21.)

events.name: National Convention of Colored Soldiers and Sailors -- called to meet at Philadelphia
events.description: Address 'To the People of the United States' dated Washington, D.C., Oct. 23, calls a National Convention of Colored Soldiers and Sailors to meet at Philadelphia, January 8th, 1867. Signers: Thomas R. Hawkins, Ohio; Geo. D. Johnson, Penna.; G. M. Arnold, Louisiana; C. B. Fisher, D.C. Correspondence to G. M. Arnold, 325 I St., Washington. (Watch topic: returning soldiers.) No Philadelphia names linked: Johnson's town is not stated.

events.name: Great Union Fair for the Book Concern, Liberty Hall -- postponed
events.description: 'Read! Read! Every Body! Fair Postponed': the great Union Fair for the A.M.E. Book Concern (announced to open Thursday Nov. 1, 1866, in Liberty Hall, Lombard St., for two weeks) is postponed because the Hall is not ready/dry; tickets good for November; the fair to last about two weeks; solid burnished silver prize cups on view in the window of the Book Store, No. 631 Pine St. 'The Fair': the paper cannot yet say whether it opens on the 1?th or 2?th [day digits unreadable]. Proceeds for the Book Concern, the paper and the last payment on the house and lot (Bishop A. W. Wayman's notice, p. 3). Donations to Rev. Elisha Weaver.
attendees: bishop (Bishop), sponsor of the fair appeal

events.name: Institute for Colored Youth -- fourteenth annual commencement
events.description: Fourteenth annual commencement of the Institute for Colored Youth at National Hall, Market street, with examination of the higher classes in the Institute building; classical preceptors Mr. E. D. Bassett and Miss Fanny Jackson. The date as printed reads like 'Thursday ... first day of O[c]tober' and is not reconcilable with the issue date; left undated [VERIFY].

events.name: Olivet Musical Association -- stated meeting and resolutions of condolence
events.location: house of Mr. John Tate, Philadelphia
events.description: Stated meeting of the Olivet Musical Association, Philadelphia, Oct. 22, 1866, at the house of Mr. John Tate; resolutions on the death of the wife of member Mr. Wm. Pegion [VERIFY surname], offered by Franklin A. Gwin [VERIFY surname]. Signed Solomon F. Mitchell, President; John W. Tate, Secretary.

events.name: Bethel A.M.E. Church -- funeral discourse for Mrs. Amelia Brooks [VERIFY]
events.description: Notice: a funeral discourse on the late Mrs. Amelia Brooks [VERIFY surname; read Bronks/Brooks at 1600 dpi] will be preached at Bethel A.M.E. Church by Rev. Wm. Moore, Sabbath afternoon, Nov. 18th; members of her Band and Class invited.

events.name: A.M.E. Zion Mission Church -- grand Sabbath School Exhibition
events.location: A.M.E. Zion Mission Church (Philadelphia presumed; place not stated)
events.description: Grand Sabbath School Exhibition in the A.M.E. Zion Mission Church, Wednesday evening Nov. 7th, 1866; doors open 7, exercises at 8; admission 15 cents, children 10 cents; proceeds for the church. Committee: Rev. T. Jones, Mr. J. Pastemah [VERIFY], Miss J. Jones, Miss H. J. Hollen [VERIFY].

events.name: Quarterly Meeting at Evesham, N.J.
events.description: Report of the quarterly meeting at Evesham, N.J. (new church; 47 added) and 13 converts 'at Mount' [place truncated]; signed Jacob M. Mitchell, Pastor. NJ circuit of the Philadelphia Conference.

events.name: Great Union Fair for the Book Concern -- opening fixed for Thursday Nov. 15; committee meeting
events.location: Liberty Hall, Lombard Street, Philadelphia (committee at the Book Store, No. 631 Pine street)
events.description: The Great Union Fair for the A.M.E. Book Concern and the Christian Recorder will open Thursday the 15th inst. (Nov. 15, 1866), to last about two weeks; 16-17 churches represented; President Mrs. Maria Hallowell, with four Vice-Presidents (not named). Committee summoned to the Book Store, No. 631 Pine street, Tuesday evening at half-past 7, Vice-Presidents to bring in books and returns. Prizes: three silver cups, a silver-mounted hat, a gilded ball, and a library register for the Sabbath school with most votes.

events.name: Institute for Colored Youth -- examination and commencement
events.location: ICY building, Shippen street west of Ninth; commencement at National Hall, Market street, Philadelphia
events.description: Examination Thursday and Friday Nov. 1-2, 1866 (Greek class under Professor Bassett, Principal; Mrs. Douglass, a teacher, ill). Teachers named: Prof. E. D. Bassett; Miss Fanny M. Jackson and Miss Mary J. Patterson (both Oberlin graduates); Mr. O. V. Catto (ICY graduate); Miss S. L. Iredell (pupil); Mr. J. Q. Allen (graduate). Four graduates received diplomas from Prof. Bassett at National Hall before about 3,000 people: Theophilus J. Minton [VERIFY], Esther E. Glasgow, Charles E. Evans, John H. Davis. Commencement date is not stated exactly; dated here by the examination.

events.name: Central Presbyterian Church -- Sabbath School Exhibition
events.description: Sabbath School exhibition Thursday the 1st inst. at the Central Presbyterian Church (pastor John B. Reeve); music department under Professor A. Boris [VERIFY]; Miss C. Davis presided at the piano; superintendent read as Mr. Evans [VERIFY].

events.name: Fair for the A.M.E. Church at Riceville, N.J. -- report of Quinn's [VERIFY] Ladies' Union Association
events.description: The members of the 'Quinn's [printed 'Qeina's'; VERIFY] Ladies' Union Association' thank the friends of Riceville for patronage at their fair of Aug. 14-16 for the church: received $216.40; expenses 54.08 [last digits uncertain]; paid to the trustees $162.38. Committee: Mrs. Rebecca Guy, Mrs. Mary Napoleon, Mrs. Charlotte Ann Cauney [VERIFY], Mrs. Jane Wates [VERIFY]; Ann Jones, President; Caroline Guy, Secretary; Rev. Henderson Davis, Pastor in Charge. N.J. circuit; names in text only per brief (not linked).

events.name: Church at Princeton, N.J. -- grand entertainment to pay off debt
events.description: Grand entertainment for the benefit of the church at Princeton (Rev. James B. Hamilton, pastor), Sunday Nov. 11; debt $150. Preachers: 10:30 a.m. Rev. Wm. Moore of Trenton; 3 p.m. Rev. Mr. Westwood of the M.E. Church of Princeton; 7:30 p.m. Rev. John R. V. Morgan of Philadelphia. Signed J. B. H.

events.name: Liberty Hall, Lombard Street -- dedication
events.location: Liberty Hall, Lombard Street between Seventh and Eighth, Philadelphia
events.description: Dedicated Monday night Nov. 12, 1866. Large three-story brick building, formerly occupied as an institute for colored youth, undergoing considerable improvement; lower story divided into stores; main hall on the second floor, 80 by 40 feet, seating 800 [VERIFY 500/800]; dining room 40 by 30 feet; upper story divided into six rooms for Odd Fellows' lodges and other societies; cost $25,000 [VERIFY figure]. Order: prayer by Rev. J. J. Clinton; Stockholders' address read by Mr. J. W. Parnell (James W. Purnell, a stockholder, per the pamphlet Address of the Stockholders of Liberty Hall); address by Rev. J. W. Hunnicutt, editor of the New Nation (Richmond, Va.); Hon. Wm. D. Kelley (D.C. suffrage bill; colored soldiers); Rev. J. Walker Jackson; short speech by Mr. O. V. Catto, 'one of the graduates of the High School'; Theodore Miller; a Freedmen's Bureau officer from Texas [name unread]. J. C. Wears (printed 'Wear') named among the speakers. White speakers (Kelley, Hunnicutt) are in the text only.
attendees: read the Stockholders' address (printed 'J. W. Parnell'); a stockholder

events.name: Mass Meeting of Colored Soldiers and Sailors of Philadelphia -- permanent organization
events.description: Reprinted report (meeting held 'last evening', date not given) of the colored soldiers and sailors of the city, in furtherance of the call for a National Convention of Colored Soldiers and Sailors at Philadelphia on Jan. 8 [1867]. Committee to correspond with the National Soldiers' and Sailors' League: Sergeant-Major A. M. Green, Sergeants D. D. Turner, J. K. Keaton [VERIFY], E. M. Burrell [VERIFY], Frank Wood, James Blount [VERIFY], Jonathan Bovard. Resolutions approving the call adopted. Addresses by Calvin Pepper, J. C. White Jr., D. B. Bowser, J. C. Bustill [VERIFY; printed 'Bustle'?], Esqs., of the State Equal Rights League; and by Sergeants D. D. Turner, A. M. Green, F. U. Revels [VERIFY], J. R. V. Morgan, Owen Dorsey, J. Bovard and others. Permanent organization, on motion of A. M. Green: Sergeant Morgan President; Sergeants Dorsey, Bovard and Revels Vice-Presidents; D. D. Turner and George Hart [VERIFY] Secretaries. Adjourned to Tuesday evening, November 20, at 8 o'clock. Topics: returning soldiers; Equal Rights League.

events.name: Bishop Campbell Bible Class and Literary Association (Union A.M.E. Church) -- officers and debate
events.location: Union A.M.E. Church, main lecture room, Philadelphia
events.description: Association instituted Tuesday Aug. 28 [1866] at Union A.M.E. Church; meets weekly Tuesday evenings. Debate: 'Are jealousy and love in harmony?' -- affirmative Mr. William H. Davis, negative Mr. Isaiah White; judges Prof. A. M. Green (critic), Mr. J. C. Wears and Mr. Redman Fauset. Officers: President Andrew Burris; Vice-President William H. Davis; Recording Scribe Catharine Fauset; Reporting Scribe Wm. Thomas Simpson; Treasurer James Mason [VERIFY]. Committee on Criticism: J. C. Wears, Redman Fauset, Wm. Thos. Simpson, Isaiah White, William H. Davis, Joseph Draper. Letter dated Philadelphia, Nov. 9th, 1866.

events.name: Jacob Rhodes lecture, St. Thomas' Church basement
events.location: basement of St. Thomas' church, Philadelphia
events.description: Mr. Jacob Rhodes to lecture Monday evening Nov. 19 on 'The fulfilment of the prophecies in 1866'; admission free.

events.name: Bishop Wayman's appointments, Nov.-Dec. 1866 (Philadelphia-area stops)
events.description: Bishop A. W. Wayman's published appointments include: Frankford, Pa., Thursday night Nov. 22; a Union Thanksgiving service at the Sullivan Street church, New York, Thursday Nov. 29 at 11 o'clock (Thanksgiving topic); Delaware and New Jersey stops; Zion church, Philadelphia, Sunday Dec. 16 afternoon; West Philadelphia Dec. 16 night; Woodbury, N.J., Dec. 17; Oxford, Pa., Dec. 18; West Chester Dec. 19; Penningtonville Dec. 20; Deep Valley Dec. 21; dedication at Germantown Dec. 22. Dates and place names read from the image; small-type day numbers should be checked against later printings.

events.name: Great Union Fair for the Book Concern -- opening at Liberty Hall
events.description: The Great Union Fair for the A.M.E. Book Concern opened Thursday Nov. 15, 1866; the ladies' tables were arranged; President Mrs. (Maria) Hallowell and the wife of Bishop Wayman were present; a display by the wife of Rev. Stephen Smith; another by the son of Rev. James Frisby [VERIFY] and another boy; a piano. Donations listed (see the 'For the Fair' article): Rev. Wm. Chase's congregation (Harrisburg Hill, Pa.), Mrs. Hollingsworth (Owego, N.Y.), Rev. Henderson Davis's people (Riceville), Rev. Wm. Moore (Trenton), Rev. Jacob Mitchell's congregation (Burlington, N.J.), Mrs. Upham; Mr. Edwin Booth gave $25. Visitors from New York (Mr. George Smith of the Sullivan Street Church; Mrs. Polk) and Washington. No proceeds figure yet.

events.name: Wedding of Rev. Elisha Weaver and Miss Martha Statts [VERIFY], and reception
events.description: Rev. Elisha Weaver (editor of the Recorder for nearly seven years, now its publisher and entire agent) married Miss Martha Statts [VERIFY surname; read Statts/Stotts] of Newark, N.J., on Wednesday evening Nov. 14, 1866, by Rt. Rev. Bishop A. W. Wayman; reception the following Thursday evening with more than 150 present (from the Evening Telegraph; also in the p3 Married column).

events.name: Masonic service at the Gloucester Church
events.location: Gloucester Church (Rev. J. B. Reeve, pastor), Philadelphia
events.description: Sunday Nov. 18, 1866, 3 p.m.: Masons' grand turnout -- knights, sir knights and Master Masons in regalia -- at the Gloucester Church, Rev. J. B. Reeve (printed 'Reeves') pastor; Masonic sermon by Rev. T. D. Miller of the Pearl Street Baptist Church. Visiting Masons from Washington named in the text (readings uncertain). Lodges not named. Parade/lodge-turnout topic.

events.name: Social, Civil and Statistical Association -- course of eight lectures, National Hall
events.description: The Executive Committee of the Social, Civil and Statistical Association of the Colored People of Pennsylvania has secured National Hall for eight lectures; the opening address on Friday evening Nov. 30, 1866, by Hon. George S. Boutwell. Invited: Frederick Douglass, Maj. Gen. O. O. Howard, Gen. B. F. Butler, Hon. Wm. D. Kelley, Mrs. F. E. W. Harper, W. W. Brown, Theodore Tilton, Hon. John A. Bingham, Senator Nye. No committee members named.

events.name: National Equal Rights League -- second annual meeting called for Washington
events.location: Washington, D.C. (call issued from the Bureau, Philadelphia, Nov. 20, 1866)
events.description: Call from the Bureau of the National Equal Rights League, Philadelphia, Nov. 20th, 1866, for the second Annual Meeting of the National Equal Rights League and National Convention of Colored Men at Washington, D.C., January 10th, 1867, 10 a.m. Executive Board: John M. Langston, President; St. George R. Taylor and Octavius V. Catto, Secretaries.

events.name: Union Fair (Book Concern Fair) in progress -- officers
events.description: Union Fair for the Publication Department / Book Concern, two weeks in progress by Dec 1. President Mrs Mary Hollowell [VERIFY]; Vice Presidents Mrs Davis (Bethel), Mrs Allen (Wesley), Mrs. Hollensworth [VERIFY] (Union), Miss Lankum [VERIFY] (Zion Mission), 'of Bethel, Wesley, Union and Zion Mission churches respectively'. Donations from Woodbury, Mount Holly (Rev Jacob Mitchell), Bridgeton (Rev Daniel Draper), Gouldtown Sabbath School (Rev Nelson H. Turpin), Camden, and a lady of Union Church, Philadelphia. 'Wesley' here unqualified (default Little Wesley lane; flagged).

events.name: Norristown A.M.E. donation surprise for Rev. H. J. Rhodes
events.description: Surprise party bringing provisions to the newly arrived pastor H. J. Rhodes: Mr and Mrs J. Able, T. Herris [VERIFY], Lober, H. Vendike [VERIFY], Mrs. E. Lewis, H. Emerson, M. A. Wilson, M. Fisher, M. Yates, A. Jones, A. Simmons [VERIFY], Miss L. Brown, H. A. Smith, C. E. Able, L. Wilkinson, M. Lewis, M. Emerson, H. E. Smith, M. Hollis [VERIFY], Mr T. Smith, D. Ross, T. Holaday, J. Ross, T. Jones, and D. Blackwell [VERIFY]. Idea suggested by sister E. Lewis.

events.name: Exhibition and festival at the A.M.E. Church, Germantown
events.description: Exhibition and festival given by Miss C. Culder [VERIFY], H. Hight [VERIFY], M. Anderson, N. Byard [VERIFY], Mrs Colder, Mr G. Coverdale [VERIFY], H. Baynard, Wm. Richardson, N. Harmon and others; presented $20 to Rev. H. J. Rhodes for an overcoat. Church at Germantown being enlarged, soon ready for dedication.

events.name: Festival at West Philadelphia for Rev. H. J. Rhodes
events.location: West Philadelphia; repeated Nov 16 at sister Green's house
events.description: Thursday and Friday evenings, Nov 15 and 16: committee Mrs Mary Grane [VERIFY] (later 'sister Green's house'), M. Rodney, S. Patterson, S. E. Jones, Miss S. Martin, assisted by Mr R. Berry, M. Williams, and J. Jones; cleared $18.15. West Philadelphia Circuit.

events.name: District Grand Lodge of Pa. and Del., Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria -- meeting called
events.location: Masonic Hall, south Eleventh street below Pine, Philadelphia
events.description: Called by order of the Grand Chief, H. M. Cropper; attest E. L. Foreman [VERIFY], Asst. Secretary. Tuesday 10 a.m.
attendees: Grand Chief (signed 'By order of the Grand Chief')

events.name: Grand Concert by the Euharmonic Coterie [VERIFY], with the Mozart Musical Society
events.location: Liberty Hall, Lombard Street below Eighth, Philadelphia
events.description: Miss Mary L. Seymour, pianist; D. W. Purvis [VERIFY] conductor; tickets 50 cents at the Recorder office. Also an editorial puff on p. 2 ('Euharmonic Coterie... grand concert at Liberty Hall').

events.name: Concert and reading for the Walnut St. A.M.E. Church, Wilmington
events.description: Committee (Wilmington; text only): Sarah Jenkins, E. J. Price, Daniel P. Hamilton, Eliza Wells [VERIFY], M. M. Collins. (Notice reprinted Dec 8, 1866.)

events.name: Burlington A.M.E. Church fair
events.description: Dec 10-24, 1866; lectures by Bishop Wayman (Dec 12), Rev. Turpin (13th), Rev Jos. Smith (19th), Rev T. Gould (20th), Rev R. P. Gibbs (missionary discourse), Rev J. Hamilton (21st). Jacob M. Mitchell, pastor.

events.name: Bordentown Circuit quarterly conference and meetings
events.description: Third quarterly Conference at Cookstown Dec 8, 2 p.m.; quarterly meeting at Allentown from Dec 15; at Bordentown Dec 22. Peter Gardner, preacher in charge.

events.name: Union Fair (Book Concern Fair) closes
events.description: Closed on Thanksgiving Day ('Thursday, the 30th ult.' as printed; Thanksgiving 1866 fell on Thursday Nov 29 -- date as computed, printed '30th'). Goods sold at auction; ladies reported to the Book Committee on Monday night; receipts about $1,836.15 [VERIFY] and the clear amount (printed '$?93.41' [VERIFY]) presented to the Book Committee for publication of the Recorder. Assisted by L. R. Seymour, 'Mulison', and William Banton [VERIFY], Superintendent of Bethel Sabbath School. Donations listed from Bethel (through Rev James Hollen) and Salem N.J. (Rev N. H. Turpin).

events.name: St. Thomas P.E. Church Sunday School concert
events.location: Liberty Hall, Lombard St. below 8th, Philadelphia
events.description: Grand Sunday School concert by St. Thomas P.E. Church; 'Rev Mr Alston's little folks'; tickets 25 and 15 cents at the A.M.E. Book Depository.

events.name: Gloucester County colored citizens' meeting on the right to vote
events.description: To raise money for a suit on the illegality of rejecting colored men at the polls. President Rev William W. Grimes; Vice President Joseph Andrews; Secretary John Andrews (also James Man as secretary); prayer by Rev H. Dickerson; Hon. Mr Scovel of Camden spoke. Committee: Joseph Andrews, Benjamin Anderson [VERIFY], Alfred Craig, Wm H. Capline [VERIFY], James Tudas [VERIFY], James Man, Wm I. Adkins. (N.J. names text only, per rule.)

events.name: Grand rally at Zion Mission A.M.E. Church
events.description: Preachers: Rev R. P. Gibbs (Union church, Coates St.) 10 1/2 a.m.; Bishop A. W. Wayman 3 p.m.; Rev E. Weaver 7 1/2 p.m. T. Gould, pastor. 'Youngest church in the city of Philadelphia, of our connection.'

events.name: Donation visit for the pastor of Wesley Church, Lombard Street
events.location: Residence of Mrs. Louisa Blackson [VERIFY], 702 Twelfth St. below Shippen, Philadelphia
events.description: For Elder J. P. Hamer, pastor of Wesley Church, Lombard Street (= Big Wesley, A.M.E. Zion, per owner's ruling). Committee: Louisa Blackson [VERIFY], Lucy Deputy [VERIFY], Mary Wolford [VERIFY], Mary Brown, Catharine Ashton.

events.name: Chester circuit quarterly meetings
events.description: Chester Dec 29-30, 1866; Horntown [VERIFY] Jan 5-6, 1867; Chichester Jan 12-13, 1867. Jeremiah Young, minister.

events.name: National Equal Rights League annual meeting and National Convention of Colored Men (call)
events.description: Call issued from the 'Bureau National Equal Rights' League, Philadelphia' (dated Nov. 20th [VERIFY], 1866) by order of the Executive Board: John M. Langston, President; George R. Taylor and Octavius V. Catto, Secretaries. Editorial (Dec 8) and W. E. M. letter (Dec 15) support it.

events.name: Union Fair prizes and Book Committee entertainment for the Fair ladies
events.description: Prize cups: Miss Ella Counsellor (member of Rev J. B. Reeves' church), Mrs Charlotte Gibson, Miss Anna George. Bethel Sabbath School won the Sabbath School Register; the Excelsior Club won the bat and ball by vote. Delmonico Brass Band played one night gratis; piano from Mr Gould's. Book Committee's entertainment for the ladies and table-tenders of the different churches at Liberty Hall.

events.name: 24th anniversary of the Union A.M.E. Church Sabbath School
events.location: Union A.M.E. Church, Coates St. below 5th, Philadelphia
events.description: A. Harris [VERIFY], Superintendent; J. C. Draper [VERIFY], Secretary.

events.name: Stroudsburg / New Hope circuit quarterly meetings and donation
events.location: New Hope, Stroudsburg, Buckingham Mountain and Attleborough, Pa.
events.description: Quarterly meetings: New Hope Dec 29; Stroudsburg Jan 5-6, 1867; Buckingham Mountain Jan [?]; Attleborough Jan 20. Richard Barney [VERIFY], pastor in charge. Dec 1 donation to him by members at Stroudsburg. He also married Wm Benson and Mrs Charlotte Lacy at Buckingham Mountain Dec 9.

events.name: Independent Order of Odd Fellows turnout and presentation of gold medal to D. B. Bowser
events.description: PROCESSION (indoor): the I.O. of O.F. appeared in full regalia and marched around the Hall. Prayer by Rev Stephen Smith; remarks by Acting Grand Master Mr William Gibson; D. B. Bowser spoke on the rise and progress of the Order and received a gold medal from W. Gibson; refreshments. Date computed: 'last Thursday night' before Sat Dec 22 = Dec 20.

events.name: St. Thomas' Church Sabbath School concert
events.description: Grand Sabbath School concert ('last Wednesday night'); Miss Alice Bowers recited 'The Black Regiment'. (Announced Dec 8 for Dec 12; reported Dec 22 as 'last Wednesday' -- date computed as Dec 19; may have been postponed. Flagged.)

events.name: Fair for the benefit of St. Thomas' P.E. Church (silver tea set vote)
events.location: New Liberty Hall, Lombard below 8th, Philadelphia
events.description: Ladies of St. Thomas' Episcopal Church; through the holidays. Committee: Miss Sally Cole, 1022 Barley St.; Miss Fanny Williams, 1920 Walnut St.; Miss Mary Wolf, 610 Pine St. (confirmed on Dec 29 reprint, f53 and f54); Miss Margaret Black, 220 [VERIFY] Quince St.; Mrs Charlotte Mills (printed 'Mille'), 1015 Lombard; Mrs Louisa Shorter, 202 Acorn Alley; Mrs Harriet Henson and Mrs Dr Wilson, 907 Lombard; Mrs Nancy Williams, 1015 Lombard (1016 on the Dec 29 reprint); Mrs Charles Gordon, 350 [VERIFY] North Third St.; Mrs Edward Collins, 669 Steiner St. (Dec 29 reprint); Mrs Thomas J. Bowers, 917 South St.; Mrs Louisa Redding, President, 1016 Fitzwater St. Silver tea set to be voted to one of: William J. Alston (St. Thomas'), J. B. Reeves (Central Presbyterian), Mr Holland (Bethel), T. D. Miller (Pearl Street), T. Gibbs (Union Church, Brown St.), J. P. Hemer [= Hamer per Dec 29 reprint] (Brick Wesley), C. Leonard (Shiloh), J. Underhue [VERIFY] (Union Baptist), Mr Watson (Little Wesley).

events.name: Grand festival for Zion Mission A.M.E. Church
events.location: Union Hall, Seventh St. above Dickerson, Philadelphia
events.description: Dec 25-27 (Christmas). T. Jones, chairman; J. Purtaman [VERIFY], secretary; T. Gould, pastor. Zion Mission's earlier surprise tea (Dec 13) at Brother Benjamin Sites' [VERIFY] with Miss L. Hoyer [VERIFY] presenting.

events.name: Colored Soldiers' and Sailors' Convention (announced)
events.description: Announced for Jan 8, 1867 in Philadelphia; Bethel Church resolved that its official board assist; letter of Isaiah Mayhugh [VERIFY], late Co. I, 8th U.S.C.T.; A. M. G. (p1) links the welcome of the returning soldiers to the streetcar exclusion. National Convention of the People in Washington, Jan 10.

events.name: Bishop Wayman's special collection at Wesley church
events.description: Bishop A. W. Wayman's appointment, Sunday Dec 30 (special collection); then Chester Dec 31. 'Wesley church' unqualified in an A.M.E. bishop's list = Little Wesley lane by default (flagged).

events.name: Mass meeting of colored citizens of Philadelphia to elect delegates to the National Convention
events.location: Liberty Hall, Lombard St. below Eighth, Philadelphia
events.description: Called in the churches and the daily papers; some white citizens present. E. D. Bassett called to order and nominated Rev Elisha Weaver temporary chairman; J. C. Bustile (= Joseph C. Bustill) temporary secretary. Committee on permanent officers: Catto, Purnell, Bassett. Dr Kent [surname only] spoke. Officers: President Isaiah C. Wear (= Wears); Vice Presidents Rev Elisha Weaver, Wm. Whipper, Rev Stephen Smith, William Still; Secretary Joseph C. Bustill. Petition to Congress on the elective franchise. Resolutions denounce exclusion from the city cars of 'men who helped fight the battles of the country' (STREETCAR) and endorse the National Equal Rights League's call. Committee to nominate delegates: William Whipper, William Still, E. D. Bassett (Still protested his own nomination). Mr J. Purnell spoke. DELEGATES as reported in the col. 5 report: Rev Stephen Smith, Rev Elisha Weaver, James R. Gordon, William Still, Rev F. P. Main [VERIFY], Rev Theodore Doughty Miller, Isaiah C. Wear, Lieut. Geo. E. Stephens, John C. Bowers, with E. D. Bassett and William Whipper added on Lieut. Stephens's motion. (The col. 3 'Delegates' local prints a garbled variant: 'J. C. W. Carr', 'James H. Gordon', 'William Whipple', 'William Sule', 'Theodore D. Miller', 'George E. Stephen'.) Officers to serve as committee on expenses.

events.name: Social, Civil and Statistical Association lecture course: Frederick Douglass
events.description: Next lecture in the Association's great course by Frederick Douglass (printed 'Frederick K. Douglass'), Thursday evening Jan 3, 1867.

events.name: Grand Rally at the A.M.E. Wesley Church, Hirst Street (Little Wesley)
events.location: A.M.E. Wesley Church, Hirst [Hurst] St., Philadelphia
events.description: Three services: 10 1/2 a.m. T. Gould assisted by J. Hollen; 2:45 p.m. Bishop A. W. Wayman assisted by G. Boyer and Wm Moore; 7 p.m. Jeremiah Turpin assisted by Elisha Weaver. Notice signed W. M. Watson (pastor). Hirst/Hurst St. = Little Wesley per owner's ruling. Same day as Bishop Wayman's 'special collection, Wesley church' (Dec 22 notice).

events.name: Sheba Lodge No. 1 (juvenile), I.O. of Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria -- deposit with Rev. Stephen Smith
events.description: Juvenile lodge under Grand Lodge No. 2; expenditures $45.75; first deposit of $300 at 6 per cent placed with Rev Stephen Smith as banker ('Thursday Dec. 21st' as printed; Thursday was Dec 20). Depositing Committee: Anna M. Hopper, Sarah A. Young, Harriet Dorsey; Treasurer Mary J. Harper. Names left unlinked because the item does not name the city.

events.name: Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria grand celebration and installation, Grand Council of Delaware
events.description: From Wilmington letter (Dec 22). Samuel Van Brakle, R.W.N.G. Chief of the I.O. of G.S. of the U.S. of North America, spoke on the Order since 1848; prayer by Rev Benjamin Scott; installed officers (Delaware; text only): Spencer M. Greenwood, Jacob Webb, Peter S. Chippey, Rev Danial P. Seaton, Rev Peter S. Williams, Joseph G. Walker, Alexander Tribbet, Moses Biddle, Robert H. Anderson, Isaac Peck, Levi Farrel.
